newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duisenberg says Germany will make grade for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg says Germany will make grade for EMU.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Monday he believed Germany would meet the entrance criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Asked by reporters whether he expected Germany to meet the entrance requirements, he said "I am confident that Germany will make it."

Countries that want to join EMU have to reach targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budgets and public debt. Germany, like many other EU countries, is facing problems cutting its deficit to the required level.

Asked whether he expected Germany to hit the 3.0 pct reference level for public deficits compared to gross domestic product exactly, Duisenberg said he expected Germany to fulfil the criteria as laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.

The treaty sets reference levels for the deficit and debt criteria but includes a clause which accepts that countries may be admitted with higher levels in special cases, such as in the event of severe economic recession.
Duisenberg, who was in Frankfurt to receive a "Banker of the Year" award, welcomed support offered to him in a speech by Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer.
Tietmeyer praised Duisenberg's policies and also said he believed he was a natural candidate for the presidency of the future European central bank.
"I welcomed Mr Tietmeyer's remarks," Duisenberg told reporters in response to a question.
